title: IEEE Project 802 and the LAN Standard
markdown:
## IEEE Project 802

In 1985, the Computer Society of the IEEE started **Project 802** to set
standards that let equipment from different manufacturers
intercommunicate. Project 802 defines the physical layer and the data
link layer functions of major LAN protocols.

Project 802 splits the data link layer of the OSI/Internet model into
two sublayers:

- **LLC (Logical Link Control)** — sits on top, common to all IEEE LAN
  protocols.
- **MAC (Media Access Control)** — sits below LLC; a separate MAC
  sublayer exists per LAN technology (Ethernet MAC, Token Ring MAC,
  Token Bus MAC, ...).

{{viz:0}}

Each MAC sublayer has its own corresponding physical layer(s)
(Ethernet physical layers, Token Ring physical layer, Token Bus
physical layer, ...), all riding on the transmission medium — mirroring
how the plain OSI/Internet model stacks Upper layers, Data link layer,
and Physical layer directly on the transmission medium.
